chapter: Regal Theatre, bebop and the Woody Herman date
title: Bebop was not danceable and singers took over
summary: Saunders liked Parker and Gillespie but says bebop's tempos and runs could not be danced to, so the public drifted and recordings turned to singers fronting bands.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Let's go back to the '40s. How did you see bebop when it started getting popular?

Well, the musician impression of it, I liked the music, and Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie and all of these people who started in that era. But it wasn't danceable. This is why it didn't live. Outrageous tempos and the passages that they would play were -- a lot of execution and running and different things like that.
So it kind of -- people had been listening to Swing and they'd been listening to danceable music. It was good jazz, but danceably.

And then when this come about, then they couldn't dance, and they stopped dancing and just started standing and looking. So -- and then it just didn't catch the fancy of the general public. Then they started to making -- recordingwise, they started to making singers the principal
thing. And then the singers who had sung with the different bands turned around and would hire the bands.
Right, right, right. Ella Fitzgerald, she had a band at one time.
Yeah, she took over Chick's band.
